info.name: HRM PLUS API
info.description:
All backend API endpoints implemented so far for HRM PLUS. One Express backend serves two route namespaces: /api/* (tenant-scoped, consumed by the tenant employee portal) and /saas/* (consumed by the public SaaS landing/signup pages and the super-admin portal). Folders below group requests by which side of the system they belong to.

Login/create requests have test scripts that auto-save tokens and ids (tenantAccessToken, saasAccessToken, employeeId, departmentId, packageId, applicationId, generatedTenantSlug, saasTenantId) into collection variables so later requests work without manual copy-pasting.

The Saas Backend > Applications (Admin) and Tenants (Admin) requests act on ids that only exist after you run Saas Frontend > Submit Application (and, for Tenants, also Saas Backend > Applications (Admin) > Approve Application) at least once — each has a description noting this. Tenants (Admin) > List Tenants only ever targets the tenant it just created (matched by slug) and deliberately never falls back to 'whatever tenant is first in the list', so it can't accidentally edit/deactivate a pre-existing tenant like the demo 'acme' one.

request.description: Basic liveness check, no auth required.

item.name: Saas Backend
item.description: Protected super-admin portal endpoints. Every request (except Saas Admin Login) needs a saas-admin access token from Saas Backend > Auth > Saas Admin Login. Suggested run order: Auth > Saas Admin Login, then Packages (Admin) > Create Package, then jump to the Saas Frontend folder to submit an application against that package, then come back here for Applications (Admin) and Tenants (Admin).

request.description: Signed with a separate secret (JWT_SAAS_ACCESS_SECRET) from tenant tokens. Saves accessToken into {{saasAccessToken}}.
Includes inactive packages, unlike the public listing.
price: 0 = free. validityDays: null = unlimited. Saves the new id into {{packageId}}.

All fields optional: name, price, validityDays, isActive. Body here only renames it (deliberately does not set isActive:false or delete it — {{packageId}} is needed by Saas Frontend > Submit Application below).

A disposable package that nothing else references, purely so Delete Package below always has something safe to delete — deliberately kept separate from {{packageId}}, which Saas Frontend > Submit Application needs to stay alive.

Deletes the scratch package created above (204 expected). To see the 409-in-use protection instead, point this at the package belonging to an approved tenant (a package referenced by {{saasTenantId}}).

item.name: Applications (Admin)
item.description: These read/act on {{applicationId}}, which is only set after running Saas Frontend > Submit Application at least once. Run that first, then come back to Get/Update/Approve/Reject here.

query.description: Pending | Approved | Rejected, omit for all

request.description: Only allowed while the application is still Pending. All fields optional: companyName, companyType, overview, numberOfEmployees, contactEmail, packageId.
Provisions a real tenant database, seeds roles, creates the tenant Admin user (password 12345678, mustChangePassword=true), and emails the login details.
reviewNote is optional. Note: if the application above was just approved, this will correctly return 409 (already Approved) — reject a different, still-Pending application to see the success path.

item.name: Tenants (Admin)
item.description: Update Tenant and Toggle Tenant Status act on {{saasTenantId}}, auto-captured by List Tenants below (run List Tenants at least once first — it grabs the newest tenant, which is the one Approve Application above just created).

exec: const match = Array.isArray(json) ? json.find((t) => t.slug === slug) : null;

console.warn('No tenant found matching {{generatedTenantSlug}} yet — approve an application first. Leaving saasTenantId untouched so Update/Toggle below cannot accidentally hit an unrelated tenant.');

request.description: Every provisioned company with package name, start/end date, and status. Finds the tenant whose slug matches {{generatedTenantSlug}} (set by Saas Frontend > Submit Application + Approve Application) and saves its id into {{saasTenantId}}. Deliberately does NOT fall back to 'the first tenant in the list' — that would risk acting on an unrelated, pre-existing tenant such as the demo 'acme' one.
All fields optional: name, companyType, overview, numberOfEmployees, contactEmail.
Flips Active/Inactive. Inactive immediately blocks every request to that tenant's subdomain (tenantResolver returns 404).
{ totalCompanies, totalPackages } for the super-admin overview page.

item.name: Saas Frontend
item.description: Public, unauthenticated endpoints consumed directly by the public landing/signup pages.

request.description: Active packages only — what the landing page shows to prospects.

formdata.value: A demo company for API testing.

request.description: Multipart form submission. logo is optional (png/jpeg/webp/svg, max 2MB). subdomainSlug must be globally unique (defaults to a timestamp-suffixed demo value). Saves the new id into {{applicationId}} and the generated slug into {{generatedTenantSlug}}.

item.name: Tenant Frontend
item.description: Auth flow used directly by the tenant login screen: two-step email/password login, session check, and forced password change.

request.description: Step 1 of login: returns { exists: boolean }. The password field is only shown client-side once this returns true.
Step 2 of login. Response includes mustChangePassword — if true, the frontend forces a password change before showing the dashboard. Saves accessToken into {{tenantAccessToken}}.

Sets a new password and clears mustChangePassword. Returns 204 with no body. IMPORTANT: {{tenantSlug}} is likely your persistent demo tenant (e.g. acme) — this genuinely changes its real login password. Run 'Revert Password' immediately after so the demo credentials stay valid for next time.
Undoes 'Change Password' above, restoring {{tenantPassword}} so the persistent demo tenant's real credentials are unaffected after running this folder end-to-end.

item.name: Tenant Backend
item.description: Protected tenant-data endpoints (employee directory, departments). Every request needs X-Tenant-Slug and a tenant access token from Tenant Frontend > Login.
